article_title: Q-Learning Lab: Teaching Reinforcement Learning Through Learner-Generated Trace Analysis
citation: Jueng, Ekkachai. (2026). Q-Learning Lab: Teaching Reinforcement Learning Through Learner-Generated Trace Analysis. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10802
title: Q-Learning Lab: a single-file bilingual browser tool for teaching tabular Q-learning
description: Q-Learning Lab is a 'single-file, browser-based, bilingual (Thai/English) tool for teaching tabular Q-learning that requires no installation and no network connection.' It renders a 5×5 gridworld with color-coded Q-values and policy arrows, exposes a live Bellman-substitution panel showing the numeric update at every step, logs every transition with the full pre-action Q-row, and exports the trace as CSV for learner-side analysis.
requirements: Runs offline from one HTML file with no external dependencies; the article states it 'runs from a double-click on any modern browser'.
constraints: Tabular Q-learning on a deterministic, fully observable, single-agent gridworld only; stochastic transitions, function approximation, continuing tasks, and multi-agent settings are 'out of scope by design'.
target_learners: undergraduates in introductory machine-learning / reinforcement-learning courses
target_learning_goals: diagnosing agent behavior against the optimal policy
key_sources: Jueng, Ekkachai. (2026). Q-Learning Lab: Teaching Reinforcement Learning Through Learner-Generated Trace Analysis. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10802
